summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis and opioid dependence was admitted after a fall during alcohol relapse. He presented with knee, back, and shoulder pain, acute alcohol intoxication, and wheezing suggestive of an asthma exacerbation. Initial evaluation ruled out fractures and intracranial injury. He was diagnosed with alcohol withdrawal syndrome and started on a Librium taper, with no complications. His asthma was managed with a steroid burst and bronchodilators. Abdominal pain was attributed to opioid withdrawal, improved with methadone restart. Imaging confirmed cirrhosis and portal hypertension with reversed portal flow and splenomegaly, but no acute findings. Liver enzymes trended downward, and he remained stable. He was discharged home on his prior medications with referrals to outpatient programs and specialist follow-up.
problems: Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
